initial_observation.encounter_context: came to the hospital with complaints related to vision and facial pain
initial_observation.chief_complaint: decrease in left-sided vision, decreased palpebral fissures, and left-sided diplopia
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The patient had left-sided eye and facial symptoms including vision decrease and diplopia, plus intense painful attacks triggered by touch, and a history of occasional headaches. Vital signs were normal and examination showed the eyeball directed downward and outward.
presenting_symptoms: intense, sharp, throbbing, sporadic, burning, and shock-like pain around the eyes, lips, nose, jaw, forehead, and scalp on the left side
attacks of sharp pain triggered by touch

evidence_items.source_text: Plain and contrast MRIs of the brain were requested, which revealed a heterogenous lobulated lesion in the region of the left side of the interpeduncular cistern extending to the prepontine cistern measuring 3 x 2.5 x 4 cm (Figures 1-3). A small component extended into the left cistern anterolateral to the pons in the left cerebellopontine angle. It was predominantly hyperintense on both the T1 weighted image (T1WI) and the T2 weighted image (T2WI), with some hypointense areas within, without significant enhancement (Figure 1, 2). Tiny T1 hyperintensities were seen diffusely scattered in subarachnoid spaces in the brain, likely to be fat (Figure 4). There was a mass effect on the left mid-brain and the left pons. Anteriorly, it abutted the left internal carotid artery. Restricted diffusion was seen (Figure 5).
In our case, the patient went for a surgical approach and had a craniotomy with the removal of the dermoid cyst and irrigation of subarachnoid spaces to remove ruptured contents and debris.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: the removal of the dermoid cyst
